cards.title: AI Agent Tightens Grothendieck Constant Bounds in Human-AI Math Collaboration Case Study
cards.why_it_matters: One of the clearest documented examples of an AI research system producing mathematically novel insights verified by domain experts — directly relevant to AI-for-science and agent capability assessment.
cards.summary: An AI research system was used to improve known bounds on the Grothendieck constant K_G — which measures hardness between combinatorial problems and their continuous relaxations — achieving bounds of 6π/11 ≤ K_G ≤ π/(2log(1+√2)) − 10⁻⁴. The paper provides a detailed case study of AI strengths and weaknesses in long-horizon mathematical research and conditions that enabled breakthrough insights.

cards.title: Surgical WAM: Action-Free Video Pretraining Lifts Surgical Robot Success Rate from 63.5% to 77.8%
cards.why_it_matters: Demonstrates a concrete, measurable benefit of world-model pretraining on action-free data for robotics — a key open question in data-efficient robot learning that generalizes beyond surgical settings.
cards.summary: Surgical WAM (built on Cosmos Policy) jointly predicts future endoscopic observations and action chunks. It pretrain on action-free surgical video, then fine-tunes on a fixed budget of action-labeled demos. Across four simulated surgical tasks, this raises average success rate from 63.5% to 77.8%, with a 20-percentage-point gain on PegTransfer; largest gains appear on contact-rich and bimanual tasks.

cards.title: SAE Latent Sets Don't Compose Like a Bag of Features, Study Finds
cards.why_it_matters: Directly challenges a common assumption in mechanistic interpretability — that SAE features combine additively — with controlled experiments on both toy models and natural text.
cards.summary: Using overlap of active SAE latent sets as a similarity measure, the authors find SAE activation sets track model-internal similarity rather than human category boundaries or typicality. Under controlled semantic modifications, there is a substantial mismatch between human judgments of conceptual change and change in the SAE active set, suggesting SAE features do not compose via simple bag-of-features semantics outside idealized settings.

cards.title: Test-Time Self-Evolving GUI Grounding via On-Policy Self-Distillation, No Human Labels
cards.why_it_matters: Addresses the open problem of post-deployment adaptation for GUI agents without human annotation, using a technically novel combination of reflection, self-distillation, and contrastive calibration.
cards.summary: The framework runs a closed loop of Exploration, Evaluation, Reflection, and Internalization. An MLLM-based Reflector evaluates grounding predictions and generates reasoning reflections; Reflection-Guided On-Policy Self-Distillation converts these into token-level supervision via a conditioned self-teacher. Contrastive Calibration prevents corrupted signals from failed explorations. Across six benchmarks, average accuracy improves 7.4% over the base model with no human-annotated ground truth.

cards.title: ALTK-Evolve vs. ACE: Token-Efficient Agentic Memory Cuts Inference Cost by ~7x on AppWorld
cards.why_it_matters: If you're building or evaluating LLM agents with episodic memory, this is a direct technical comparison of two self-improving agent systems on the same benchmark, with concrete cost-accuracy tradeoffs.
cards.summary: Both ACE and ALTK-Evolve convert an agent's past trajectories into reusable lessons injected at inference time — no weight updates. Key difference: ACE injects the full playbook every step; ALTK-Evolve selects a priority-weighted subset per task and model. On AppWorld, ALTK-Evolve matches or beats ACE on accuracy while using ~40% of ACE's tokens on strong models and ~14% on weak models.
